t:
For salaries and expenses, including the transfer and hire of motor vehicles, of the District of Columbia Public Defender Service, as authorized by the National Capital Revitalization and Self-Government Improvement Act of 1997, $44,011,000, of which $344,000 shall remain available until September 30, 2022 for costs associated with relocation under a replacement lease for headquarters offices, field offices, and related facilities:  Provided, That notwithstanding any other provision of law, all amounts under this heading shall be apportioned quarterly by the Office of Management and Budget and obligated and expended in the same manner as funds appropriated for salaries and expenses of Federal agencies:  Provided further, That the District of Columbia Public Defender Service may establish for employees of the District of Columbia Public Defender Service a program substantially similar to the program set forth in subchapter II of chapter 35 of title 5, United States Code, except that the maximum amount of the payment 
made under the program to any individual may not exceed the amount referred to in section 3523(b)(3)(B) of title 5, United States Code.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for the salaries and expenses of the D.C. Public Defender Service, with provisos on OMB apportionment and an optional voluntary separation incentive program for its employees. The tempting reading is that the reference to a District of Columbia entity or to a "program" for employees signals outside involvement, but no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue or object over any federal decision. The only interaction is budgetary apportionment by OMB, which is internal funding administration.
fable.s: all amounts under this heading shall be apportioned quarterly by the Office of Management and Budget and obligated and expended in the same manner as funds appropriated for salaries and expenses of Federal agencies

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes funding for salaries and expenses of the District of Columbia Public Defender Service. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government in the decision-making process. The mention of employees and their benefits is internal to the agency's operations and does not constitute public participation.
qwen_block.s: For salaries and expenses, including the transfer and hire of motor vehicles, of the District of Columbia Public Defender Service... $44,011,000

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision that funds the DC Public Defender Service and has OMB apportion the money. Both are actions taken inside the federal government. The authority to create an employee program is internal personnel administration, not rulemaking or consultation with outside parties. No state, expert, member of the public or other outside party takes part in any decision here.
opus.s: all amounts under this heading shall be apportioned quarterly by the Office of Management and Budget and obligated and expended in the same manner as funds appropriated for salaries and expenses of Federal agencies
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **No**: nothing in the section brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision.

1. **The tempting reading:** Two parts look procedural. The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) apportions the funds, and the DC Public Defender Service may set up a program for its employees. Neither counts. OMB apportionment is an action inside the federal government. The employee program is internal personnel administration. It involves no rulemaking, hearing, comment period, advisory body or consultation with outside parties.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the establishment of an employee relocation benefit program for the District of Columbia Public Defender Service. This is an internal administrative matter regarding employee compensation and does not involve consultation or coordination with parties outside the government (such as the general public, states, or private organizations) in the making of a federal decision. The actors involved are the government agency and its employees.
qwen_chat.s: the District of Columbia Public Defender Service may establish for employees of the District of Columbia Public Defender Service a program substantially similar to the program set forth in subchapter II of chapter 35 of title 5, United States Code
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Public Defender Service is an independent entity or that the employees are "outside" the federal government, and thus establishing a benefits program for them constitutes participation. However, the District of Columbia Public Defender Service is a government entity (part of the District government, which is treated as a local government but here the funds are appropriated for its salaries and expenses in a manner similar to federal agencies, and the employees are public servants). More importantly, the text describes the internal administration of employee benefits (relocation payments) for a specific government workforce. It does not involve consulting with the general public, states, tribes, or private entities to make a federal decision. It is an internal administrative provision regarding how appropriated funds are used for employee compensation.
